answer.rationale: The durable memory and experimental evidence establish that promotional pricing aimed at price-sensitive SMB creates short-term acquisition gains but fails retention (exp_73 showed -12% 30-day retention, no survival past first renewal). This makes it misaligned with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. In a competitive price-cut scenario, matching discounts would replicate this failure at scale. Instead, activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to meaningful first action—a retention-correlated signal. Combined with the proven onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31, exp_86: +3% 30-day retention), this creates a defensible, non-commoditizing response: make the product itself stickier and faster-to-value, reducing churn risk through engagement rather than price capitulation. Referral_incentives (memory_57) are effective for established customers but do not address immediate churn in price-sensitive SMB. Enterprise_sales_assist aligns with memory_44 but does not address the current SMB base under competitive threat. A standard_experiment scope allows rapid validation in at-risk cohorts without full-scale commitment, preserving optionality if results prove insufficient.
